units.title: Adventure
units.intro: Grammar: gerunds (-ing as a noun), infinitives (to + verb), participles, and the future continuous.

cards.title: Gerunds, infinitives and participles
rule: A **gerund** (verb + -ing) works as a noun: ***Camping** is fun.* After prepositions and verbs like *enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, can’t help*, use the gerund: *I enjoy **climbing**.*
An **infinitive** (to + verb) follows verbs like *want, decide, hope, plan, attempt, agree*: *They decided **to camp**.* It also shows purpose: *She went out **to buy** bread.*
**Participles as adjectives:** -ing describes the cause (*an **amazing** trip*); -ed describes the feeling (*We were **amazed***).

examples.text: The story was horrifying; we were horrified.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: The manager rejected the proposal because he felt that ________ details were provided to support the budget.

steps.text: The blank modifies the noun 'details'. 'Details' is a plural countable noun (indicated by the '-s' ending).
Uncountable quantifiers like 'little' and 'a little' cannot modify plural countable nouns. 'Too few' is the correct quantifier for countable nouns in a negative context.
Tigrinya speakers often conflate 'few' and 'little' as both translate to 'ውሑድ' or 'ቅሩብ'.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: Which of the following sentences contains a pluralization error?

steps.text: 'Crisis' is a noun of Greek origin.
National exams frequently test irregular non-English plurals.

cards.answer: The school board discussed several educational crisises.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Although the construction project has been delayed, ________ progress has been made this week.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Progress' is an uncountable noun in English. It cannot be pluralized and cannot pair with countable quantifiers.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
'A few' and 'many' are strictly countable. 'Few' is also countable. 'Some' can modify both countable and uncountable nouns, making it the only grammatically viable option here.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Progress' (ዕብየት/ምስጓም) ዘይቝጸር ስም (uncountable noun) እዩ። 'Many' ን 'a few' ን ንዝቝጸሩ ስማት ጥራይ ስለ ዝኾኑ ምስ 'progress' ክኸዱ ኣይኽእሉን። 'Some' ግን ምስ ክልቲኦም ስለ ዝኸይድ ቅኑዕ መልሲ Option C እዩ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: The police ________ investigating the robbery that occurred near the national bank.
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze the grammatical structure**
'Police' is a collective noun that is grammatically plural and always takes a plural verb.

**Step 2: Identify the matriculation trap**
Because 'police' does not end in '-s', many non-native speakers mistake it for a singular noun and pair it with singular verbs like 'is' or 'was'. This is a highly targeted agreement trap in the ESSLCE.

**Step 3: Tigrinya Explanation (ትርጉም)**
'Police' (ፖሊስ) ዝብል ስም ክትርእዮ ከለኻ ናይ ነጸላ (singular) ይመስል እምበር፡ ብሰዋስው ግን ወትሩ ብዙሕ ቁጽሪ (plural) ተገይሩ ስለ ዝውሰድ ድሕሪኡ ዝመጽእ ግሲ 'are' (Option B) ክኸውን ኣለዎ።

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: I feel like _______ to the library.
cards.why: The phrasal verb **'feel like'** is always followed by a **gerund** (the -ing form of the verb). It is used to express a desire or inclination to do something.

cards.title: Future continuous
rule: **will be + -ing** = an action in progress at a future time: *This time tomorrow we **will be climbing** the mountain.* It is also used for planned future events: *I **will be meeting** him at noon.*

examples.text: At 8 tomorrow I will be travelling to Keren.

examples.fix: At 8 tomorrow I will be travelling.

cards.title: Find and correct the error
cards.problem: Find and correct the error: "At 8 tomorrow I will travelling."

steps.text: **Step 1: Recall the rule.** **will be + -ing** = an action in progress at a future time: *This time tomorrow we **will be climbing** the mountain.* It is also used for planned future events: *I **will be meeting** him at noon.*
**Step 2: Test the sentence.** "At 8 tomorrow I will travelling." breaks this rule.
**Step 3: Correct it.** "At 8 tomorrow I will be travelling."

cards.answer: At 8 tomorrow I will be travelling.

cards.title: Memory tip
body: **After a preposition, always -ing.** The **-ing** thing causes the **-ed** feeling.

cards.title: Unit summary
body: Gerunds act as nouns and follow prepositions and verbs like enjoy/avoid/finish; infinitives follow verbs like want/decide/hope and show purpose. -ing adjectives describe causes, -ed adjectives feelings. Future continuous (will be + -ing) describes an action in progress at a future time.

glossary.meaning: A verb + -ing used as a noun.

tips.text: **After a preposition, always -ing.** The **-ing** thing causes the **-ed** feeling.
